heroLead: Structural strength and insulation in one panel. Insulspan replaces purlins, beams, trusses, sarking, bulk insulation and plasterboard with a single install, and the underside is a finished Surfmist ceiling.
overviewPara1: Insulspan is a three-in-one insulated roof panel: a Colorbond top skin, an EPS-FR foam core and a 0.5 mm Surfmist steel underside that is your finished ceiling. Engineered single spans run up to 5.7 m with no purlins.
overviewPara2: Designed for Australian conditions, Insulspan insulated roof panels remove the need for purlins, beams, trusses, mesh, sarking, bulk insulation and plasterboard, and cut the number of trades you need on site.
overviewPara3: We make Insulspan to order in Silverdale NSW, in four thicknesses from 50 mm to 125 mm and three profiles, for patios, carports, pavilions and home roofs.

faqLead: Straight answers to what builders, owner builders and certifiers ask us about Insulspan.

faq.a: Insulspan is an insulated roof panel made by Quick Built Systems in Silverdale NSW. Each panel is a Colorbond top skin, an EPS-FR foam core and a 0.5 mm Surfmist steel underside, so one panel is the roof, the insulation and the finished ceiling.

faq.q: How far can an Insulspan panel span?
faq.a: Up to 5.7 m as a single span on an open patio (open on 3 sides): a 75 mm or 100 mm panel in N1. Spans drop as the wind class rises: 5.3 m in N2, 4.0 m in N3 and 3.3 m in N4 for a 75 or 100 mm panel. These come from the Ross Engineers patio engineering, drawing 22-1204-ST. For a partly enclosed patio, or a size the table does not list, talk to us first. The full table is on this page.

faq.q: What thicknesses and R values are there?
faq.a: Four thicknesses: 50 mm (R1.39), 75 mm (R2.09), 100 mm (R2.78) and 125 mm (R3.48). Panel weight runs from 8.8 to 9.5 kg/m².
Always Surfmist. The top skin comes in the Colorbond colours shown on this page; the underside ceiling is the same clean off-white on every panel.
Monospan (trapezoidal ribs), Corrugated, and Corro / Corro, which is corrugated top and underside. All three share the same structural core and span table.
Yes, to BAL-29. We do not supply Insulspan for BAL-40 or Flame Zone sites. Fire hazard indices to AS/NZS 1530.3 are ignitability 0, spread of flame 0, heat evolved 0 and smoke 2-3.

faq.q: Can I fit downlights and ceiling fans?
faq.a: Yes. There are install guides for LED downlights, ceiling fans (with the fan fixing plate kit) and suspended ceilings under Insulspan panels in the downloads on this page.
Insulspan is made to order, so allow about 4 weeks to make, plus about a week for freight. Alyspan beams and posts we buy in take about 2 weeks, plus about a week for freight.

Direct from us on 1300 132 787 or sales@quickbuiltsystems.com.au for panels made to your job, as a complete DIY patio kit at patiokits.com.au, where the patio designer prices your size for your postcode, or as an Insulspan patio kit ordered through Bunnings. Insulspan is not kept in store, but any Bunnings can special order it.

faq.q: What about wind classes above N4, or cyclonic sites?
faq.a: Our documents cover N1 to N4 with engineering. Sites above N4, and cyclonic sites in wind Regions C and D, are engineered per project and priced with the job.

faq.q: How many beams and posts will I need?
faq.a: It depends on the spans. The panel span table on this page sets how far apart the beams can be for your wind class and panel thickness, and the beam span tables set the post spacing.

faq.q: What is the plastic film on the underside?
faq.a: Pull it off once the panels are up and in place.

faq.q: Can Insulspan be joined to another brand's roof panels?
faq.a: No. We cannot join our panels to another brand's panels, such as an existing patio roof from another maker. The roof has to be our system.

faq.q: Can you add an acoustic layer, such as ply, under the panels?
faq.a: No, we don't do this. The panel is the roof, the insulation and the ceiling in one.
